note: National programs are real organizations; local listings are illustrative samples. Always confirm current eligibility.

programs.name: State Assistive Technology Act Programs
programs.what_they_offer: Every U.S. state and territory has an Assistive Technology Act program. Many offer device demonstrations, short-term loans, and used-equipment reuse or exchange services, and offerings differ by state.
programs.how_to_apply: Find your state's program through the Association of Assistive Technology Act Programs and ask about loans, demos, and reuse. Availability and eligibility vary by state.

programs.name: Pass It On Center
programs.what_they_offer: A national center that supports assistive technology reuse programs across the U.S. and helps families learn about device reuse, exchange, and recycling options.
programs.how_to_apply: Visit the website to learn about device reuse and to find reuse programs in your state. Contact them to ask for current guidance.

programs.name: Variety - the Children's Charity
programs.what_they_offer: A children's charity with local chapters that supports children with disabilities, including adaptive equipment and mobility programs. Award amounts and programs vary by chapter, so check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Find your regional chapter through the website and ask about current programs, eligibility, and application steps.

programs.name: Challenged Athletes Foundation
programs.what_they_offer: A national nonprofit that provides grants for adaptive sports equipment and training for people with physical disabilities, including young athletes. Grant amounts vary, so check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Review the grant information on the website and submit an application with the information requested. Confirm current eligibility and deadlines.

programs.name: UnitedHealthcare Children's Foundation
programs.what_they_offer: A nonprofit that offers grants to help families pay for health-related services and items not covered, or not fully covered, by insurance. Eligibility, items, and amounts vary, so check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Read the current eligibility requirements on the website and apply online if your family qualifies. Confirm deadlines and what is covered before applying.

programs.name: Chive Charities
programs.what_they_offer: A charity that gives grants to individuals and organizations, including some that support children facing medical or mobility needs. Programs and amounts vary, so check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Visit the website to review current grant categories and application instructions. Confirm eligibility before applying.

programs.name: Easterseals Local Affiliates
programs.what_they_offer: Easterseals is a national disability services organization with local affiliates. Some affiliates offer equipment loan or assistive technology services, and offerings vary by location.
programs.how_to_apply: Use the website to find your local Easterseals affiliate and call to ask whether they have an equipment loan or assistive technology program.

programs.name: Lions Clubs (local clubs)
programs.what_they_offer: Many local Lions Clubs run community service projects, and some keep loan closets or help with vision-related needs. Offerings vary by club.
programs.how_to_apply: Find a nearby club through the website, then contact the club and ask whether they lend equipment or can help with your need.

programs.name: Rotary Clubs (local clubs)
programs.what_they_offer: Some local Rotary clubs support community projects and individual families in need. Support and amounts vary by club, so check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Find a nearby club through the website and contact the club about whether they offer help with equipment or local projects.

programs.name: Kiwanis Clubs (local clubs)
programs.what_they_offer: Kiwanis is a service organization focused on children and communities, and some local clubs may help with family needs or community projects. Support varies by club.
programs.how_to_apply: Find a local club through the website and contact it to ask whether they support equipment requests.

programs.name: Friends of Man
programs.what_they_offer: A charitable organization that has helped people with disabilities with mobility and adaptive equipment needs. Offerings and amounts vary, so check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Search for the organization's official site and confirm current eligibility and the application process before applying.

programs.name: Front Range Gear Swap
programs.what_they_offer: A sample community swap where Denver-area families trade outgrown wheelchairs, standers, and adaptive bikes. Volunteers help check fit and basic safety.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. In a real program you would post what you have and what you need and arrange a fitting with your therapist.

programs.name: Puget Sound Loan Closet
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Seattle-area loan closet offering short-term loans of mobility and bath equipment while families wait for insurance approval.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real program would ask for a therapist's note and a pickup appointment.

programs.name: Rose City Mobility Share
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Portland reuse program that refurbishes donated equipment and matches it to growing kids, with a therapist checking the fit.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real program would ask for a clinician's measurements and a short intake form.

programs.name: Bay Area Adaptive Swap
programs.what_they_offer: A sample San Francisco swap meet where families exchange outgrown adaptive gear, with an OT on site for questions.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. Real swaps typically ask you to register ahead and bring item details and photos.

programs.name: Sunshine State of Mind Equipment Fund
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Los Angeles-area fund that helps families cover gaps after insurance for equipment and access modifications. Amounts vary — check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real fund would ask for a denial letter or cost estimate and a clinician's note.

programs.name: Harbor Light Loan Closet
programs.what_they_offer: A sample San Diego loan closet with wheelchairs, walkers, and bath chairs available for up to several months while you wait for your own.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real program would ask for a short intake and a therapist's measurements.

programs.name: Desert Sky Reuse Exchange
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Phoenix-area exchange that cleans, repairs, and matches used equipment to children and young adults.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real exchange would ask for a clinician's recommendation.

programs.name: Live Oak Little Wheels Swap
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Austin swap where families trade outgrown kids' mobility gear and share fitting tips.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real swap would ask you to register and list your equipment.

programs.name: Bayou Ramp Builders Fund
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Houston-area fund that supports volunteer-built ramps and small home access projects. Amounts vary — check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real program would ask for a home assessment and proof of ownership or landlord approval.

programs.name: North Star Equipment Library
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Minneapolis equipment library where families borrow gear for weeks or months, including winter-friendly options.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real library would ask for a referral and an appointment for fitting.

programs.name: Lakeshore Gear Swap
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Chicago swap meet where caregivers trade outgrown adaptive equipment and meet other families.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real swap would ask you to register ahead of the event.

programs.name: Buckeye Reuse Collective
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Columbus reuse collective that refurbishes and redistributes donated equipment to children and young adults.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real program would ask for a therapist's recommendation and measurements.

programs.name: Huron Valley Loan Closet
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Ann Arbor loan closet with short-term loans of mobility and bath equipment while families wait for insurance.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real closet would ask for a short intake and an appointment.

programs.name: Peach State Mobility Fund
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Atlanta-area fund that helps families cover the gap between insurance and the cost of mobility equipment. Amounts vary — check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real fund would ask for an estimate and a clinician's letter.

programs.name: Music City Loan Closet
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Nashville loan closet with wheelchairs, walkers, and bath chairs available on short-term loan.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real program would ask for a short form and a therapist's note.

programs.name: Triangle Little Movers Swap
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Raleigh-area swap where families trade outgrown mobility gear and share growth tips.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real swap would ask you to register and share photos of your item.

programs.name: Capital Region Reuse Exchange
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Washington, DC exchange that repairs and redistributes donated equipment to children and young adults.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real program would ask for a clinician's recommendation and an appointment.

programs.name: Liberty Bell Access Fund
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Philadelphia fund that helps families with access modifications and equipment not fully covered by insurance. Amounts vary — check current guidelines.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real fund would ask for a quote and a clinician's letter.

programs.name: Beantown Gear Swap
programs.what_they_offer: A sample Boston swap where caregivers trade outgrown adaptive equipment and share advice on school and home setups.
programs.how_to_apply: Sample listing for demonstration. A real swap would ask you to register ahead and bring item details.

programs.name: National AMBUCS — Amtryke therapeutic tricycle program
programs.what_they_offer: Local AMBUCS chapters fundraise to provide Amtryke adaptive tricycles to riders who can't ride a standard bike; a family's ability to pay is not what decides eligibility.
programs.how_to_apply: Ask your child's PT or OT for an evaluation and recommendation (required), then contact your nearest AMBUCS chapter through the national chapter directory.

programs.name: Wheel to Walk Foundation
programs.what_they_offer: Helps children 20 and under with a documented disability get equipment and therapies insurance won't cover, paying the vendor directly. Does not cover deductibles, co-pays, or home/vehicle modifications.
programs.how_to_apply: Apply online with a therapist or physician letter of medical necessity, the vendor quote, and the insurance denial letter. Serves families in the Pacific Northwest and California; confirm current eligibility.

programs.name: McLindon Family Foundation (adaptive bikes)
programs.what_they_offer: A Baton Rouge nonprofit that gives free adaptive bikes fitted to each child, working with pediatric rehab clinics, and swaps in a bigger bike when a child outgrows theirs.
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through the foundation's website with your child's therapist; check whether they currently serve families outside Louisiana.

programs.name: California Children's Services (CCS) and its Medical Therapy Program
programs.what_they_offer: California's program for kids with qualifying conditions, such as cerebral palsy, can cover medical equipment, and its Medical Therapy Program provides PT/OT, often at school-based Medical Therapy Units.
programs.how_to_apply: Ask your pediatrician or county CCS office about a referral; check eligibility rules on the DHCS site.

programs.name: Regional Center of the East Bay (Alameda & Contra Costa counties)
programs.what_they_offer: California's regional center for the East Bay serves eligible people with developmental disabilities, including cerebral palsy, and can help with services, some equipment and respite when other sources don't cover them.
programs.how_to_apply: Call RCEB intake to request an eligibility assessment; services are planned in an Individual Program Plan (IPP).

programs.name: Connecticut Tech Act Project (assistive technology loans)
programs.what_they_offer: Connecticut's statewide assistive technology program (Department of Aging and Disability Services) offers low-interest loans to buy AT and connects families to equipment programs.
programs.how_to_apply: See the CT Tech Act page on portal.ct.gov or call the program to ask about loans and device options.

programs.name: NEAT Marketplace (restored equipment)
programs.what_they_offer: Restores donated adaptive devices and medical equipment so families can buy them for less than new.
programs.how_to_apply: Browse what's available on their site or call to ask about specific equipment.

programs.name: MassMATCH Assistive Technology Regional Centers (hosted by Easterseals Massachusetts)
programs.what_they_offer: Free device demonstrations and a lending library of equipment, software and toys, from low-tech to high-tech, that Massachusetts residents can borrow for up to 30 days. Try before you buy, or bridge a gap while insurance decides. Boston center at 89 South Street, with a second center in Worcester.
programs.how_to_apply: Create a free account at massmatch.at4all.com, browse the inventory and request up to 5 devices, or contact the Boston center to schedule a visit.

programs.name: REquipment Durable Medical Equipment & Assistive Technology Reuse
programs.what_they_offer: A program of MassMATCH (the Massachusetts Assistive Technology Act program) that cleans and restores donated home medical equipment and assistive technology and provides it free to Massachusetts residents, including children. Helpful if insurance won't cover an item, you need a backup while a chair is in the shop, or you need something short term.
programs.how_to_apply: Search the online inventory on the REquipment website, then call or email (info@requipmentma.org) to request an item.

programs.name: Catastrophic Illness in Children Relief Fund (CICRF)
programs.what_they_offer: A Massachusetts Department of Public Health fund that can help families of children and youth under 22 with medically related expenses not covered by insurance, including medical equipment and supplies. Home modifications and accessible vehicles are also considered, with limits and a sliding scale.
programs.how_to_apply: Review the eligibility and covered-expense pages on mass.gov, then apply after the expenses are incurred; the CICRF Commission makes the final decision.

programs.name: Minnesota STAR Program device loans
programs.what_they_offer: Minnesota's federally funded assistive technology program lends devices free so families can try before they buy, gather data for a funding request, or borrow while their own device is repaired. Short-term loans run up to 45 days, with a very limited number of open-ended loans.
programs.how_to_apply: Contact STAR or one of its partners, or browse the MN AT4ALL online lending library and submit a loan request; pick up or have the device shipped at no cost.

programs.name: PACER Simon Technology Center Assistive Technology Lending Library
programs.what_they_offer: More than 1,500 assistive technology items, including education, communication and daily living products plus iOS apps. Membership is free for Minnesota families, and families can borrow 4 items and 4 apps at a time.
programs.how_to_apply: Complete PACER's online membership form, then reserve items through the MyTurn library catalog; items can be mailed or picked up by appointment in Bloomington.

programs.name: Minnesota STAR Program assistive technology reuse and Device Exchange
programs.what_they_offer: STAR's reuse services help pass along assistive technology a family no longer needs, by selling, exchanging or donating it, and its Device Exchange lists online sites where you can donate, sell or find used equipment.
programs.how_to_apply: Visit STAR's Reuse page to find the Device Exchange listings, or contact STAR for help finding used equipment.

programs.name: Washington Assistive Technology Act Program (WATAP) device lending
programs.what_they_offer: Washington's statewide assistive technology program lends devices for 21 days (with short extensions) so families can try before they buy or bridge a gap during repairs, and ships anywhere in Washington. WATAP also offers device demonstrations, evaluations and training for people with disabilities and their circle of support. There is a nominal borrowing fee based on the device's value and maintenance cost.
programs.how_to_apply: Start at WATAP's Borrow a Device page or contact WATAP; ask about devices for your child's mobility, vision, hearing or communication needs.

programs.name: Northwest Access Fund low-interest assistive technology loans
programs.what_they_offer: A nonprofit serving Washington, Oregon and Idaho that offers low-interest loans (not grants) to buy assistive technology, plus free one-on-one financial coaching. WATAP partners with the Fund on AT financing.
programs.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Fund's AT loan page or call 1-877-428-5116 to ask about current rates, limits and whether a family member can apply on a child's behalf.

programs.name: Bridge Disability Ministries: Meyer Medical Equipment Center
programs.what_they_offer: An Eastside nonprofit center that provides essential mobility and medical equipment, refurbishing donated items such as wheelchairs and walkers for people who need them.
programs.how_to_apply: Visit Monday-Thursday, 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., at 15411 NE 95th St in Redmond, or call (425) 628-1751 / email equipment@bridgemin.org; ask about cost and whether pediatric sizes are available.
